title: SQL injection in user search endpoint
description: The /api/search endpoint concatenates the untrusted q parameter directly into a raw SQL string, allowing an authenticated user to inject arbitrary SQL. Proof of concept: GET /api/search?q=' OR '1'='1 returns the full users table.
root_cause: search_users in api/search.py does not parameterize the q parameter before passing it to run_raw, allowing SQL injection.
intended_behavior: The developer intended to filter the users table by a case-insensitive substring of the display name.

trace.description: reads the request query parameter q with no validation
interpolates q into a SQL string via f-string
executes the concatenated SQL against the primary database

conditions.description: Any authenticated user; no elevated role required.

execution.attacker_perspective: An authenticated low-privilege user with a normal account.
instructions: Log in with any valid account
Send GET /api/search?q=' OR '1'='1 with the session cookie
execution.expected_result: The response contains every row of the users table rather than the caller's own matches.

remediation.strategy: Use parameterized queries so user input is never part of the SQL string.

code_changes.fixed_code: cursor.execute('SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name LIKE ?', (f'%{q}%',))

likelihood.reason: Trivial to exploit; needs only a valid low-privilege session and a single request.

impact.reason: Full read of the users table, including columns above the caller's access level.

confidence.reason: Complete data flow verified from entrypoint to sink; no intervening mitigation found.

reason: The /api/export endpoint flagged by the hunt pass was investigated and rejected: export_csv in api/export.py routes through the same require_role('admin') decorator as the UI (api/export.py:9), so a low-privilege user cannot trigger it. The claimed trace omitted that decorator.
